assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Three separate @TableTest methods: reisDiscountPercentage (ladder), discountByPassengerType (eligibility), and rollingTripCount (rolling window)

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: In discountByPassengerType table: 'Child flat discount | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20' shows 20% regardless of trip count

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: reisDiscountPercentage table shows all tiers: 0% tier {1, 4}, 5% tier {5, 9}, ..., 40% tier (max) {40, 50}

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: rollingTripCount table includes 'Trip just outside window | [31] | 0' (31 days excluded), but no row testing exactly 30 days. The @Description notes this as an open question: 'is the 30-day boundary inclusive?...confirm with the product team before implementing the boundary check.'

assertions.text: Eligibility uses human-readable values (yes/no or equivalent) rather than raw true/false. TypeConverter or similar mechanism mentioned.
assertions.evidence: Passenger types are expressed as human-readable enums (ADULT, SENIOR, CHILD); @TypeConverter is present for parsePriorTrips

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Each value set in reisDiscountPercentage contains min/max for exactly one tier with no overlaps: {1, 4} → 0%, {5, 9} → 5%, {10, 14} → 10%, etc.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value. The 'every fifth trip' rule creates tiers; the table should express tiers, not enumerate boundaries.
assertions.evidence: reisDiscountPercentage uses value sets for ticket ranges: {1, 4}, {5, 9}, {10, 14}, {15, 19}, {20, 24}, {25, 29}, {30, 34}, {35, 39}, {40, 50} — one row per tier

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables. A price application table (if present) should test the arithmetic (base price × discount → final price) without re-enumerating which ticket counts map to which tier.
assertions.evidence: Tier-to-discount mapping appears only in reisDiscountPercentage method; discountByPassengerType reuses the tier concept without re-enumerating mappings; no separate price application table

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All three test methods have @DisplayName: 'Reis discount percentage from trip count', 'Discount by passenger type', 'Rolling 30-day trip count'

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the discount ladder structure, eligibility rules, or application context. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: @Description on reisDiscountPercentage explains 'Trip count is the number of single tickets...First discount (5%) applies when the count reaches 5'; on discountByPassengerType explains adults/seniors vs children flat 20%; on rollingTripCount explains the window measurement — all provide context beyond table content

assertions.text: TypeConverterSources is used for at least one human-readable conversion (yes/no, or rolling window notation).
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter public static List<LocalDateTime> parsePriorTrips(String value) converts rolling window notation '[1, 15, 29]' to List<LocalDateTime>

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All three methods follow the order: @DisplayName, then @Description, then @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description uses triple-quoted strings: @Description("""...""") on all three methods

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone — rather than silently omitting zone. The requirement explicitly says 'regardless of the zones you travel in'.
assertions.evidence: discountByPassengerType table columns are: Scenario | Passenger type | Trips in last 30 days | Discount percentage? — Zone is silently omitted, not shown with a value set

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row of the eligibility table, since they follow identical discount rules. Not enumerated as separate rows with the same outcome.
assertions.evidence: discountByPassengerType table uses {ADULT, SENIOR} as a value set in multiple rows: 'No discount yet (adult/senior) | {ADULT, SENIOR} | {1, 4} | 0' and subsequent rows

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table: 0% (tickets 1-4), 5% (5-9), 10% (10-14), 15% (15-19), 20% (20-24), 25% (25-29), 30% (30-34), 35% (35-39), and 40% (40+). Not just a subset of tiers.
assertions.evidence: reisDiscountPercentage table includes all 9 rows: 0% tier {1, 4}, 5% tier {5, 9}, 10% tier {10, 14}, 15% tier {15, 19}, 20% tier {20, 24}, 25% tier {25, 29}, 30% tier {30, 34}, 35% tier {35, 39}, 40% tier (max) {40, 50}

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows (e.g. separate rows for 'tier kicks in' and 'tier holds'). One tier = one row.
assertions.evidence: Each discount tier in reisDiscountPercentage is expressed as one row: '0% tier | {1, 4} | 0', '5% tier | {5, 9} | 5', etc.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or an integer 'Days ago' column) rather than using absolute dates, making the table readable without needing to know the reference date.
assertions.evidence: rollingTripCount table uses 'Prior trips (days before purchase)' column with relative values [1, 15, 29], [31], etc.; @TypeConverter converts to LocalDateTime relative to PURCHASE_TIME
